meta.title: Habits
meta.description: A local-first habit tracker: streaks, a month grid and weekly targets, with no server at all. The first document whose core is calendar arithmetic; it does that arithmetic by hand because the notation has no date operators yet.

name.message: Give the habit a name (up to 40 characters).

target.message: Target is between 1 and 7 days per week.

name.message: Give the habit a name (up to 40 characters).

target.message: Target is between 1 and 7 days per week.

today.description: The calendar date of `context.now`, as YYYY-MM-DD. The runtime's `now` is UTC; see the pressure on time zones.

todayDay.description: Days since 1970-01-01, computed from the civil date by hand because the notation has no date operators (ticket 21).

weekStartDay.description: Day number of the first day of the current week.

calendar.description: Every day in a window around today, converted once so every other definition looks dates up here instead of repeating the arithmetic.

windowDates.description: The dates that count for streaks and rates: the last `daysBack` days including today.

habitStats.description: Per habit: streaks, rates and the last seven days. One pass over the marks per habit; the calendar is memoized.

weekDone.description: Marks this week, capped per habit at its target.

weekCompletionBp.description: Integer basis points so tests are exact; formatted with `percent` for display.

monthGridStart.description: Day number of the first cell: the week-start on or before the first of the month.

monthGrid.description: Six weeks of cells covering the current month, for the habit page.

toggle-mark.description: Marks or unmarks one habit on one date. Reads `habitId` and `date` from the call. Future dates are ignored.

children.content: Everything stays in this browser. No account, no server.

tests.name: today is derived from the runtime clock and converted to a day number
tests.description: 2024-03-15 is 19797 days after 1970-01-01 and a Friday (weekday 5 with Sunday = 0).

tests.name: the calendar converts day numbers back to dates, including a leap day
a streak survives the month boundary and a leap day
tests.description: Marks every day from Feb 27 to Mar 15 (a leap day inside): an 18-day streak ending today; 18 of the last 30 days is 6000 bp; 5 marks in the week of Mar 11.

tests.name: a streak broken yesterday is zero; the best streak is remembered
today unmarked keeps yesterday's streak alive
marks older than the window do not count for streaks or rates
tests.description: daysBack is 30: 2024-02-15 is the first day that counts; Feb 10 to Feb 14 are outside.

tests.name: week completion depends on the week start: Monday
tests.description: Sunday 2024-03-17. With Monday as week start the week is Mar 11 to 17; Read has 4 of 5, Walk 3 of 3 (a fourth mark does not count): 7 of 8 = 87.5% → 8750 bp.

tests.name: week completion depends on the week start: Sunday
tests.description: Same marks, same Sunday; with Sunday as week start the week is only Mar 17: Read 1 of 5, Walk 0 of 3.

tests.name: no habits means zero completion, never a division by zero
the month grid starts on the week start before the first of the month
tests.description: Tree test: March 2024 starts on a Friday; with Monday as week start the grid opens on Feb 26 and those cells are blank spacers. The heading names the month.

tests.name: the index page lists habits with their streaks and the week bar
the weekly summary channel renders one line per habit
toggling a mark twice leaves no mark; a future date is ignored
tests.description: Action scenario: transforms only. The third call targets tomorrow and must not add a mark.

tests.name: adding a habit assigns a sequential id, resets the draft, toasts and navigates
an invalid draft is refused with the schema's message
